title: parseGoJson blames a package-level panic on every already-failed test, not just the one that died
property: a test that finished with an explicit fail event keeps its own assertion error even if a different test later panics in package output
property_test: a test that failed on its own does not inherit another test's panic
input: TestA: output '    a_test.go:3: got 1, want 2' then fail; TestB: run only; package-level output 'panic: boom'
expected: TestA error = AssertionError 'got 1, want 2' (only the unfinished TestB may take the panic)
actual: TestA error is re-parsed from its lines plus the package output and becomes type 'panic', message 'boom'
evidence: The comment says 'a panic printed after the test's own lines lands in package output', i.e. it is meant for the test that was running; but the condition only checks outcome === 'failed' and that the test's own lines lack 'panic:', so every failed test with a t.Error is overwritten.
